# isValidDomain

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is a domain name.</link-summary>

<web-summary>isValidDomain() — Checks whether a value is a domain name. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>net/path</code></p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function isValidDomain(domain: string): domain is string;
```

Labels separated by single dots, with no leading or trailing dot or hyphen and no empty label. It is a syntax check: whether the domain resolves is another question.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type     | Description                                       |
| :-------- | :------- | :------------------------------------------------ |
| `domain`  | `string` | The string to check for valid domain name syntax. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is a domain name; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `domain` to `string` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
isValidDomain("example.com"); // => true
isValidDomain("sub.example.co.uk"); // => true
isValidDomain("-example.com"); // => false
isValidDomain("example..com"); // => false
isValidDomain("example.com."); // => false
isValidDomain(""); // => false
```
